hints: Suppose you pick one number from each list. The interval covering them is [smallest pick, largest pick]. To make it narrower, which pick is worth changing?
Keep one pointer per list. A min-heap gives the smallest current pick, and you track the current maximum. Advancing the minimum's list is the only move that can shrink the window.

1. Push the first value of every list into a min-heap (value, list, index) and record the max.
  2. Pop the smallest; the window [min, max] is a candidate, keep it if it is strictly narrower.
  3. If that list has no next value, stop.
  4. Otherwise push its next value and update the max.
  5. Return the best window.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Merge all values with their list id, sort, and try every pair of start/end positions, checking whether all lists are covered.

approaches.name: Better
approaches.idea: Sort all (value, list) pairs and use a sliding window that counts how many lists are covered.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: K-way merge: a min-heap of one pointer per list plus a running max.

explain: For [[1,8,20],[4,9,15],[6,12,30]] the first picks are 1, 4, 6, giving window [1,6]. Pop 1, push 8: picks 4, 6, 8 give [4,8], which has the same width 4, so the earlier [1,6] stays. Pop 4, push 9: picks 6, 8, 9 give [6,9], width 3, the new best. Later windows [8,12], [9,20], [12,20] and [15,30] are all wider, and popping 15 empties the second list, so the search stops with [6,9]. Using strict < keeps the earlier window on ties, and since the minimum only grows, earlier means smaller lo.
recognize: Several sorted lists and 'one element from every list' → a k-way min-heap with a running max.
python:
class Solution:
    def tightestWindow(self, lists: List[List[int]]) -> List[int]:
        h = [(l[0], i, 0) for i, l in enumerate(lists)]
        heapify(h)
        mx = max(l[0] for l in lists)
        best = [h[0][0], mx]
        while True:
            v, i, j = heappop(h)
            if mx - v < best[1] - best[0]: best = [v, mx]
            if j + 1 == len(lists[i]): return best
            nv = lists[i][j + 1]
            mx = max(mx, nv)
            heappush(h, (nv, i, j + 1))
